title: Least Squares Separate (LSS) Analysis for fMRI Data
text: primary function lss(), takes data Y, trial design X, experimental regressors Z, optional nuisance regressors.
code: library(fmrilss)  # 1. Generate synthetic data set.seed(123) n_timepoints <- 120 n_trials <- 15 n_voxels <- 50  # Trial design matrix (X): one column per trial X <- matrix(0, n_timepoints, n_trials) onsets <- round(seq(from = 5, to = n_timepoints - 10, length.out = n_trials)) for(i in 1:n_trials) {   X[onsets[i]:(onsets[i] + 4), i] <- 1 } colnames(X) <- paste0("Trial_", 1:n_trials)  # Experimental regressors (Z): intercept and condition-specific effects # These are experimental regressors we want to model and get beta estimates for, # but not trial-wise (e.g., condition differences, block effects) Z <- cbind(Intercept = 1, LinearTrend = scale(1:n_timepoints, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE))  # Nuisance regressors: e.g., 6 motion parameters Nuisance <- matrix(rnorm(n_timepoints * 6), n_timepoints, 6)  # Data (Y): timepoints x voxels # (Simulate some effects for demonstration) true_betas <- matrix(rnorm(n_trials * n_voxels, 0, 1.5), n_trials, n_voxels) Y <- Z %*% matrix(c(10, -0.2), 2, n_voxels) +       X %*% true_betas +      Nuisance %*% matrix(rnorm(6 * n_voxels, 0, 2), 6, n_voxels) +      matrix(rnorm(n_timepoints * n_voxels, 0, 0.8), n_timepoints, n_voxels) colnames(Y) <- paste0("Voxel_", 1:n_voxels)   # 2. Run LSS analysis  # Example 1: Basic LSS with default intercept # If Z is NULL, an intercept is automatically added. beta_estimates <- lss(Y, X)  # Example 2: LSS with experimental regressors (intercept + condition effects) beta_fixed <- lss(Y, X, Z = Z)  # Example 3: LSS with experimental regressors and nuisance regression beta_clean <- lss(Y, X, Z = Z, Nuisance = Nuisance)  # Example 4: Use the super-fast, parallelized C++ implementation beta_fast <- lss(Y, X, Z = Z, Nuisance = Nuisance, method = "cpp_optimized")  # The result is a (trials x voxels) matrix of beta estimates print(dim(beta_fast)) #> [1] 15 50 print(beta_fast[1:5, 1:4])

text: Estimates single-trial response amplitudes GLMsingle procedure (Prince et al., 2022): library-based HRF per voxel, GLMdenoise noise regressors chosen cross-validation, voxel-wise fractional ridge regression chosen cross-validation repeated conditions. implementation reorganises computation (per-run factorisation, single pass data products per stage, compiled cross-validation sufficient-statistic R^2) much faster reference implementation computing estimator.

title: GLMsingle single-trial response estimation — glmsingle
text: Y Data: list time x voxel matrices (one per run), one time x voxel matrix runs giving run row. design Either list time x condition 0/1 matrices, one per run (GLMsingle's format; 1 marks trial onset), data frame columns run, onset (seconds; must TR grid) condition. Repeated conditions drive cross-validation. matrix Y, event run IDs matched runs data order. list Y, ascending event run IDs correspond list order. tr Repetition time seconds. stimdur Trial duration seconds. runs Run identifier per row Y Y single matrix. hrf_library Optional time x HRF matrix sampled TR (first row onset). Default: glmsingle_hrf_library(). want_library Fit HRF library per voxel (otherwise canonical HRF used every voxel). want_glmdenoise Derive select GLMdenoise noise regressors. want_fracridge Fit fractional ridge model (type D). fracs Ridge fractions (0, 1] evaluate. single value skips cross-validation uses fraction. n_pcs Maximum number noise PCs evaluate. Capped, warning, available noise-pool rank across runs. Empty rank-zero pools use zero PCs skip PC-count cross-validation. pcstop Stopping factor choosing number PCs. value <= 0 uses -pcstop PCs without cross-validation. xval_scheme List integer vectors runs held together cross-validation fold. Default: leave one run . session_indicator Integer session per run, used z-score betas within session cross-validation. Default: one session. extra_regressors Optional list (one per run) time x regressor nuisance matrices (e.g. motion), NULL. max_poly_deg Polynomial drift degree, scalar one per run. Default: round(run_seconds / 120) GLMsingle. brain_thresh Two numbers: percentile mean volume fraction ; voxels brighter product may enter noise pool. brain_r2 -R^2 (percent) bright voxels enter noise pool. Default: estimated tail threshold. fewer two distinct finite -R^2 values, uses common value (zero none finite). Thresholds estimated denoising used. brain_exclude Optional logical vector voxels exclude noise pool (FALSE excludes). pc_r2_cutoff -R^2 voxels summarise PC-count cross-validation. Default: estimated tail threshold. pc_r2_cutoff_mask Optional logical vector restricting voxels. want_percent_bold Express betas percent signal change mean volume. want_autoscale Rescale ridge betas best match unregularised betas (type D). extras_in_denoise user extra regressors enter GLMdenoise ridge fits: "always" (default, recommended) "with_pcs" (least one PC used; GLMsingle's behaviour). zero_sd_cv Treatment voxels whose reference betas zero variance within session cross-validation: "zero" (default) "python" (reproduce GLMsingle's Python behaviour). singular run's trial regressors linearly dependent: "error" (default, GLMsingle) "pinv" (minimum-norm solution warning). frac_alpha fractions map ridge penalties: "fracridge" (default; GLMsingle's grid interpolation) "exact" (solve fraction equation exactly; experimental). full_glmbadness Compute PC-count cross-validation every voxel instead voxels decide PC count. Estimates identical; glmbadness diagnostic filled voxels. chunk_size Number voxels processed time (GLMsingle's chunklen). Lower reduce peak memory. n_threads Threads per-voxel C++ loops (0 = OpenMP default). Results depend thread count. Matrix products use BLAS library's threads; use n_threads > 1 single-threaded BLAS, two thread pools compete cores. verbose Print progress messages.

title: GLMsingle single-trial response estimation — glmsingle
text: Defaults reproduce GLMsingle (Python, commit 1ab54a6) except GLMsingle internally inconsistent: extras_in_denoise = "always" keeps user extra regressors every GLMdenoise ridge fit; GLMsingle (Python) drops zero noise PCs used, including cross-validation reference. "with_pcs" reproduces GLMsingle. zero_sd_cv = "zero" gives voxels zero beta variance weight cross-validation; GLMsingle's -place division helper treats inconsistently across candidates. "python" reproduces . -R^2 threshold uses deterministic two-Gaussian mixture fit small variance floor (GLMsingle's MATLAB code); GLMsingle's Python fit unseeded. want_percent_bold applies model types (GLMsingle always scales types C D). Computation double precision (GLMsingle uses single). HRF indices 1-based; betas trials x voxels. FIR diagnostic model, hrfmodel = "optimize", wantlss, bootstrap modes, figures file outputs implemented.

title: GLMsingle single-trial response estimation — glmsingle

code: set.seed(1) tr <- 1; n_time <- 120; n_vox <- 40 design <- lapply(1:3, function(r) {   D <- matrix(0, n_time, 6)   onsets <- seq(5, 95, by = 8)   D[cbind(onsets, rep_len(sample(6), length(onsets)))] <- 1   D }) Y <- lapply(design, function(D) {   X <- apply(D, 2, function(s) stats::filter(s, glmsingle_hrf(3, tr),                                               sides = 1, circular = FALSE))   X[is.na(X)] <- 0   100 + X %*% matrix(rnorm(6 * n_vox, 2), 6) + matrix(rnorm(n_time * n_vox), n_time) }) fit <- glmsingle(Y, design, tr = tr, stimdur = 3, n_pcs = 2, verbose = FALSE) dim(fit$typed$betasmd) #> [1] 36 40

code: # \donttest{   library(fmrihrf)   set.seed(3)   Tlen <- 180; V <- 4   sframe <- sampling_frame(blocklens = Tlen, TR = 1)   H <- cbind(exp(-seq(0, 30, length.out = Tlen)/5),              exp(-seq(0, 30, length.out = Tlen)/7))   sbhm <- sbhm_build(library_H = H, r = 2, sframe = sframe, normalize = TRUE)   onsets <- seq(8, 140, by = 12)   design_spec <- list(sframe = sframe, cond = list(onsets = onsets, duration = 0, span = 30))   hrf_B <- sbhm_hrf(sbhm$B, sbhm$tgrid, sbhm$span)   rr <- fmrihrf::regressor(onsets = onsets, hrf = hrf_B, duration = 0, span = 30, summate = FALSE)   Xr <- fmrihrf::evaluate(rr, grid = sbhm$tgrid, precision = 0.1, method = "conv")   alpha_true <- rnorm(ncol(sbhm$B))   Y <- matrix(rnorm(Tlen*V, sd = .6), Tlen, V)   Y[,1] <- Y[,1] + Xr %*% alpha_true   out <- lss_sbhm(Y, sbhm, design_spec)   out2 <- lss_sbhm(Y, sbhm, design_spec,                   match = list(topK = 2, soft_blend = TRUE),                   return = "amplitude")   names(out) #>  [1] "matched_idx"       "matched_name"      "margin"            #>  [4] "alpha_coords"      "shape_mode"        "prepass_fallback"  #>  [7] "fallback_low_conf" "trial_basis_map"   "event_amplitude"   #> [10] "event_duration"    "event_run"         "diag"              #> [13] "topK_idx"          "weights"           "alpha_mode"        #> [16] "amplitude"         # }
